_comment: Declared deviations and withdrawals: differences and absences that are known,
explained and expected. Read conformance/deviations.py for why this exists.
Every entry MUST name: kind ('deviation' or 'withdrawal'), scope (cases, and for
deviations ports/stages/optionally paths), reason, basis (user decision or bus
frame), declared date, owner, and removed_when - the EVENT that retires it.
kind 'deviation': the case IS run and a difference against the golden is expected.
kind 'withdrawal': the sample was taken out, the case is NOT run - there is nothing
to diff, and the report must show it as NOT verified, never as verified-with-a-
difference. A withdrawal must name specific cases, never '*'.
A date is not an exit condition; an entry without removed_when is a permanent
loosening in disguise. An entry that matches nothing where it applies is STALE.

deviations.reason: The ports carry the passport page registration (page_registration/: template locator, quad fit, line refinement, line dewarp) and reproduce the canvas of both internal-passport cases exactly (borders.canvas and deskew.canvas match). What does not converge bitwise is the line refinement: the reference uses cv2.createLineSegmentDetector, which neither gocv 0.43 nor OpenCvSharp4 binds, so both ports find their line evidence with Canny+HoughLinesP; and the 4-parameter IRLS fit runs on a hand-written Levenberg-Marquardt instead of scipy.optimize.least_squares (trf). A slightly different refinement homography moves the field boxes by 1-7 px on Go (median 1, p90 3) and 1-10 px on .NET, shifts detector confidences by up to 0.03, and on each case flips one character of one field where the crop edge crosses a glyph. The Kotlin/JVM port binds LSD and matches bitwise, so it is not listed. Measured 2026-09-21 on the models-v6 goldens; both ports are deterministic run to run (RANSAC seeded). D-01 (MRZ re-read ladder) and D-02 (normalized dates ahead of the goldens) retired the same day: all three ports carry the ladder now, and the goldens were regenerated with the canonical dates in them, so both entries matched nothing. In this tree both passport cases are withdrawn (W-01, W-04), so this entry records the ports' state and matches nothing here until a synthetic replacement returns the cases.
deviations.basis: user decision of 2026-09-19 (release 4.5.0 in one window with the ports; a residual that cannot be made pixel-exact is declared with its measured size rather than left to hold the release); measured on the ports' conformance reports of 2026-09-21
deviations.removed_when: an LSD binding becomes available in the port's OpenCV wrapper and the line refinement is re-run through it, or the reference switches its line evidence to a detector the ports can call bitwise - then this entry goes stale and must be deleted

deviations.reason: On this case with models-v7 the template locates page 2 only; page 3 is cut straight from its Borders quad ('borders-spare') in the reference and in the Kotlin port alike. Everything before that cut matches (sources, page-2 registration method and 26 inliers, native scale 0.4954, page-2 line refinement to the 5th decimal, the same dewarp decision). The spare page itself does not: the line refinement finds 30 LSD segments on it against 31 in the reference - a different input picture, since LSD is the same binding on both sides - so its refinement homography and its dewarp decision differ, and field boxes move by 1-4 px (38 values in fields.bbox, 19 in words, 45 in the view model; the recognised text is identical). Narrowed to the spare page's cut, not pinned: the likeliest source is quad_fit's RANSAC, which draws with Kotlin's own PRNG instead of NumPy's PCG64 (QuadFit.kt says so and names this as the place to revisit); warp interpolation is the other candidate. Measured 2026-09-26/27 by a traced run against the reference. The sample is withdrawn from this tree (W-01); the entry applies where the case runs.
deviations.basis: user decision 2026-09-26 (release 4.6.0 with weight set models-v7); the 4.5.0 rule that a residual which cannot be made pixel-exact is declared with its measured size rather than left to hold the release (decision of 2026-09-19)
deviations.removed_when: quad_fit's RANSAC in the Kotlin port draws the same samples as the reference (a PCG64 port), or the spare-page cut is otherwise shown to match - then this case runs clean and the entry goes stale and must be deleted

deviations.reason: With the models-v8 text-field detector, one field box of this sample comes out 1 px apart: the x0 of Birth_place_en (box 9) is 611 in the reference and 610 in all three ports, identically. The reference's value before rounding is 610.988, so this is NOT a rounding edge like the retired D-04 - the ports' detector output for this one box is about half a pixel lower. The word split of that field inherits it: its two word boxes move by 1-3 px and one confidence by 0.002 (7 values in all, the same on every port); the recognised text is identical and every other box and stage of the case match. Cause not established; the likeliest is the ONNX Runtime version - the goldens were written on onnxruntime 1.22.0, the ports run 1.21. The sample is withdrawn from this tree (W-02); the entry applies where the case runs.
deviations.basis: user decision 2026-09-28 (release 4.6.1 with weight set models-v8, decision #137); the 4.5.0 rule that a residual which cannot be made pixel-exact is declared with its measured size rather than left to hold the release (decision of 2026-09-19). Replaces D-04, which went STALE with these weights
deviations.removed_when: the goldens and the ports run the same onnxruntime version and the box matches (then this entry goes STALE - delete it), or the next weight set moves the difference away
